name: Line Dancing
notes: Line Dancing style pack (Doc 04 template). Genuinely solo — like samba no pé, zero partner nodes: the whole point of a line dance is that everyone dances it alone, together. TWO THREADS, both credited as curriculum, because line dancing's story is usually told half-missing: (1) the honky-tonk/country thread that boomed in the 80s-90s (Tush Push, created by Jim Ferrazzano in 1980; the post-'Achy Breaky Heart' explosion of 1992), and (2) the Black American soul line dancing thread — the Electric Slide (choreographed by Ric Silver in 1976 to Marcia Griffiths' 'Electric Boogie'), the Cupid Shuffle (Cupid — Bryson Bernard, 2007, the dance IS the song's instructions), the Wobble — a living tradition at cookouts, weddings and soul line socials that predates and parallels the country boom. Choreographer credits are the norm in this culture (step sheets carry authors' names) — this pack keeps that norm. Vocabulary first (grapevine, shuffle, pivot, kick-ball-change), then whole dances by name and author.

seasons.finale: Film the four building blocks back to back: grapevine, shuffle step, pivot turn, kick-ball-change — clean both directions.
Film the Electric Slide, full sequence, all four walls — and say Ric Silver's name on camera.
Film the Tush Push through all four walls — Jim Ferrazzano's step sheet, your boots.
Film the Cupid Shuffle and one more soul line dance — the wall turns, the groove stays.
Dance in an actual line: a country bar, a wedding, a cookout, a soul line social — anywhere the floor moves as one.

attributes.name: Count ear L1
attributes.test: count 8s out loud through one full track, restarting cleanly at every phrase — line dances live on the phrase

attributes.name: Pivot balance L1
attributes.test: 10 half-pivot turns each direction on the balls of the feet, no stumble on the landing

nodes.name: Counts, phrases, and walls
checkpoints: a line dance is a fixed sequence (16, 32, 64 counts) that repeats facing a new wall each time
count the phrase, not just the beat — the sequence restarts with the music's sentence
4-wall, 2-wall, 1-wall: know which dance you're in before the first wall turns

nodes.name: One format, every genre
checkpoints: line dances run to country shuffle, disco, funk, soul, and pop — the format doesn't care about genre
same grapevine, different groove: let each track change HOW you step, not WHAT you step
the DJ's job at a line night is to move the room between worlds — go with them

nodes.name: Two threads: honky-tonk and soul line dancing
checkpoints: line dancing's story has two great threads, and both deserve their names
the country/honky-tonk thread boomed after 'Achy Breaky Heart' (1992) turned line dances into a phenomenon
the Black American soul line dancing thread — Electric Slide, Cupid Shuffle, the Wobble — lives at cookouts, weddings and soul line socials, and it predates and parallels the country boom
telling only half this story is the common mistake; this pack doesn't make it

nodes.name: Step sheets — a culture that credits its choreographers
checkpoints: line dance culture writes its dances down as step sheets, and step sheets carry the choreographer's NAME — crediting is the norm here, not the exception
when you learn a dance, learn its author; when you teach it, pass the name along
thousands of credited dances exist — this pack teaches a canon, the culture holds the library

nodes.name: Grapevine
nodes.anchor: the most-used step in all of line dancing
checkpoints: side, behind, side, touch (or scuff, or hitch — the fourth count is the flavor slot)
travel flat and smooth; the crossing foot goes BEHIND
both directions until neither needs thought
mistakes: crossing in front (that's a different step)
drifting forward instead of pure sideways

nodes.name: Shuffle step (triple)
checkpoints: step-together-step in two counts — the line dancer's triple
low and smooth: boots skim
forward, back, and sideways — all three flavors

nodes.name: Pivot turns (quarter & half)
checkpoints: step forward, pivot on both balls of the feet to face the new wall
weight ends clearly on one foot — the next count needs to know
this is how walls turn; own it and no dance can lose you

nodes.name: Kick-ball-change
checkpoints: kick, land on the ball, change weight — one crisp '&' count of syncopation
small kick, quick feet; it's a rhythm accent, not a punt
the step that makes line dances feel funky instead of marched

nodes.name: The Electric Slide
nodes.origin: choreographed by Ric Silver in 1976 to Marcia Griffiths' 'Electric Boogie' — soul line dancing's worldwide anthem
checkpoints: grapevine right, grapevine left, walks back, rock and lean, quarter turn — 18 counts, four walls
the lean is the soul of it: settle in, don't rush off
danced at more weddings and cookouts than any dance alive — learn it once, belong everywhere
mistakes: turning the wrong way on the wall change (everyone does, once, publicly)

nodes.name: Tush Push
nodes.origin: created by Jim Ferrazzano (1980) — the honky-tonk thread's most-danced step sheet
checkpoints: heel touches, the hip bumps, shuffles forward, the half-pivot — the full sheet, wall by wall
the hip section swings easy — it's called the Tush Push for a reason
at country bars this one starts without announcement; the floor just knows

nodes.name: Cupid Shuffle
nodes.origin: Cupid (Bryson Bernard), 2007 — the song IS the step sheet: 'to the right, to the right…'
checkpoints: four rights, four lefts, four kicks, walk-it-by-yourself quarter turn
the walk section is YOUR four counts — groove them, don't waste them
soul line dancing's modern classic; the artist told you the steps himself

nodes.name: Cotton-Eyed Joe
nodes.origin: traditional — the tune goes back through American folk history long before any single choreographer; the kick-and-stomp line version is folk process at work
checkpoints: cross-kicks and back-shuffles in eights — simple, loud, communal
stomp like you mean it; this one is allowed to be rowdy
a dance with no author is a dance with ten thousand — that's folk tradition, name it as such

nodes.name: Four dances, four walls — filmed, credited
checkpoints: film all four named dances, each through at least four walls
announce each dance's name AND its choreographer before you start it — the step-sheet norm, honored
no stopping when you go wrong: find the wall, rejoin the count, keep dancing — that's the real skill

nodes.name: Dance in a real line
checkpoints: a country bar's line night, a wedding, a cookout, a soul line social — anywhere the floor moves as one
join a dance you don't know and survive it by watching feet — the line teaches
notice the feeling this format exists for: alone, together
